content.text:
We need answer only JSON. Need extract product-review semantic claims. Need parse source. Need exactly one primary/secondary pair per claim, independently polarity, evidence_span exact continuous substring. Multiple claims maybe. Need no inference from star rating. If no supported product claim exists empty. We need identify claims about product. Product seems screen protector. Review title: "Good, but needs more items to assist in installation process". Source text includes install perfect for phone. 3 glass protectors included, but both attempted install on husband's phone did not have same easy installation even followed same process/directions. Normally use military grade glass protectors & one on my phone seems no issues so far. Seems quality on other two screens wasn't same as mine. Attempted contact replacement... no emails. Hopefully replacement/communication.

We need choose taxonomy pairs. Primary topics: usability_installation, product_quality, function_performance, reliability_durability, convenience_value etc.

Claims:
1. "My install was perfect for my phone." This is positive about installation ease/outcome? Usability_installation/ease_of_use? Or positioning_alignment? "install was perfect" could be installation process/ease. primary usability_installation, secondary ease_of_use? Maybe installation_difficulty? Perfect suggests ease. Evidence exact: "My install was perfect for my phone." polarity positive. But maybe "install was perfect" not specifically ease. Could be positioning_alignment? Hmm.

2. "3 glass protectors were included" This is product_quality/accessory_condition? Or convenience_value? Included accessories. It's a factual claim about accessory condition? Product_quality accessory_condition maybe. Polarity neutral? It states 3 included. Could be positive? Neutral factual. Evidence "3 glass protectors were included". But secondary accessory_condition? yes.

3. "but both we attempted to install on my husband’s phone did not have the same easy installation even though we followed the exact same process and directions." This is usability_installation/ease_of_use or installation_difficulty. Negative. Evidence exact substring. Could be "both we attempted to install on my husband’s phone did not have the same easy installation even though we followed the exact same process and directions" (including but? Evidence span exact continuous substring; can include "but both..."?). Need ensure exact substring from source. Source has "but both we attempted..." yes. Claim: installation not same easy. Primary usability_installation; secondary ease_of_use? Or installation_difficulty. Since "did not have same easy installation" indicates difficulty. Taxonomy has installation_difficulty. Use that? Polarity negative. Evidence maybe "both we attempted to install on my husband’s phone did not have the same easy installation even though we followed the exact same process and directions" exact.

4. "We normally use the military grade glass protectors & the one on my phone seems to have no issues whatsoever so far." Claim about general performance? No issues so far. primary function_performance secondary general_performance. Polarity positive. Evidence exact substring. Could be positive. But "military grade" maybe quality? "no issues whatsoever so far" performance/durability. Function_performance general_performance.

5. "Seems like the quality on the other two screens wasn’t the same as mine." Product_quality/material_build_quality? Negative. Evidence exact. Primary product_quality; secondary material_build_quality? Or defective_on_arrival? "quality ... wasn't same" material build quality. Polarity negative.

6. "Attempted to make contact for replacement and added all information through their help website. After submitting successfully it says we’ll send you an email to verify, but I’ve received no emails." This is about customer service, not product claim? Taxonomy other_unknown? The claim about replacement/communication not product? Could be reliability? Not sure. We might omit because not product claim. But maybe "Attempted to make contact for replacement" implies product defective? But already product_quality? We shouldn't invent. Could include other_unknown/uncategorized? The instruction: Extract product-review semantic claims. A review may contain zero/multiple claims. For every claim choose taxonomy. If no supported product claim exists return empty. Customer service issues maybe not product claim. We should not include. "Hopefully I’ll get a replacement..." no.

Need decide how many claims. Likely 5 claims. Need check exact evidence substrings. Ensure no modification. Source_text: 
"Good, but needs more items to assist in installation process\nMy install was perfect for my phone. 3 glass protectors were included, but both we attempted to install on my husband’s phone did not have the same easy installation even though we followed the exact same process and directions. We normally use the military grade glass protectors & the one on my phone seems to have no issues whatsoever so far. Seems like the quality on the other two screens wasn’t the same as mine. Attempted to make contact for replacement and added all information through their help website. After submitting successfully it says we’ll send you an email to verify, but I’ve received no emails. Hopefully I’ll get a replacement or some communication soon."

Need exact substring with apostrophe? It uses husband’s with curly apostrophe. Need copy exact. Evidence_span exact continuous substring. We can include curly. In JSON ensure valid. Need ensure "we’ll" etc if used.

Potential claim from title: "needs more items to assist in installation process" This is about missing installation accessories. Primary usability_installation, secondary installation_accessories? Negative? Title says Good, but needs more items to assist in installation process. Evidence span: "needs more items to assist in installation process" exact. Polarity negative? It's a need/missing items. Primary usability_installation, secondary installation_accessories. Should include? Title is part of source? The source_text includes title line at beginning. Yes. It is a product claim. So include as claim. Polarity negative? "needs more items" indicates lacking. Could be negative. Evidence: "needs more items to assist in installation process" (without Good, but). That is exact substring. Maybe include. This is about installation accessories. Good.

Now claim 1 "My install was perfect for my phone." Could be positive about ease. But "My install was perfect" may be positioning alignment? Actually install perfect = installation went perfectly. Primary usability_installation secondary ease_of_use? or installation_difficulty? Since "perfect" positive. I'd use ease_of_use. But secondary "ease_of_use" not exactly installation ease? It is ease of use. Could use installation_difficulty negative? No, positive implies no difficulty. Use ease_of_use.

But careful: "My install was perfect for my phone." The phrase "install" refers installation of screen protector. Primary usability_installation. Secondary ease_of_use. Polarity positive.

Claim "3 glass protectors were included" maybe accessory_condition. Primary product_quality, secondary accessory_condition. Polarity neutral. The fact included 3 maybe positive? It says 3 included; no sentiment. Could be neutral.

Claim "but both we attempted to install on my husband’s phone did not have the same easy installation even though we followed the exact same process and directions." Primary usability_installation; secondary installation_difficulty. Negative. Evidence should include? "both we attempted to install on my husband’s phone did not have the same easy installation even though we followed the exact same process and directions" exact. It starts with "both"; source "but both..." We can exclude "but " as evidence. "both we attempted..." is exact continuous? Source: "included, but both we attempted..." After "but " yes substring "both we attempted..." exact. Fine.

Claim "We normally use the military grade glass protectors & the one on my phone seems to have no issues whatsoever so far." Could be two? Military grade glass protectors maybe material quality? But "one on my phone seems to have no issues whatsoever so far" is performance/durability. Primary function_performance general_performance positive. Evidence could be "the one on my phone seems to have no issues whatsoever so far". It is exact substring? Source: "& the one on my phone seems..." Starting with "the one..." yes. Good. Maybe include "We normally use the military grade glass protectors & the one..."? Better narrow.

Claim "Seems like the quality on the other two screens wasn’t the same as mine." Primary product_quality material_build_quality negative. Evidence exact.

Could there be claim "both we attempted to install ... did not have same easy installation" also implies defective_on_arrival? Maybe not. We should not double? Could have product_quality defective? But likely one claim about installation difficulty.

Could include replacement communication no emails as other_unknown/uncategorized? The schema says other_unknown if no supported product claim. But review includes customer service. "Attempted to make contact for replacement and added all information through their help website. After submitting successfully it says we’ll send you an email to verify, but I’ve received no emails." This is not product claim; it's service. We should omit. But if asked "product-review semantic claims" maybe only product claims. Omit.

Need ensure taxonomy version? Not in output. Only claims array. Must adhere schema. AdditionalProperties false. We can output {"claims":[...]}.

Need decide if include title claim. The title is in source_text before newline. Evidence "needs more items to assist in installation process" exact. Polarity negative? The phrase "needs more items" is negative about included accessories. Maybe primary usability_installation, secondary installation_accessories. Yes.

Let's enumerate final claims:

1. primary: usability_installation, secondary: installation_accessories, polarity: negative, evidence: "needs more items to assist in installation process"
2. primary: usability_installation, secondary: ease_of_use, polarity: positive, evidence: "My install was perfect for my phone."
3. primary: product_quality, secondary: accessory_condition, polarity: neutral, evidence: "3 glass protectors were included"
4. primary: usability_installation, secondary: installation_difficulty, polarity: negative, evidence: "both we attempted to install on my husband’s phone did not have the same easy installation even though we followed the exact same process and directions"
5. primary: function_performance, secondary: general_performance, polarity: positive, evidence: "the one on my phone seems to have no issues whatsoever so far"
6. primary: product_quality, secondary: material_build_quality, polarity: negative, evidence: "Seems like the quality on the other two screens wasn’t the same as mine."

Check exact substring for claim 4: Source: "3 glass protectors were included, but both we attempted to install on my husband’s phone did not have the same easy installation even though we followed the exact same process and directions." The substring "both we attempted..." yes. Include husband’s curly. The source uses ’ in husband’s. Need copy. In final JSON, can include curly apostrophe. Ensure no trailing period maybe okay. Evidence can be without period. It is exact continuous substring. Good.

Claim 5: Source: "We normally use the military grade glass protectors & the one on my phone seems to have no issues whatsoever so far." Substring "the one on my phone seems to have no issues whatsoever so far" exact. Yes.

Claim 6: Source: "Seems like the quality on the other two screens wasn’t the same as mine." exact. yes.

Potential issue: Claim 3 "3 glass protectors were included" maybe not claim if neutral. But okay. Primary product_quality accessory_condition? The taxonomy secondary accessory_condition under product_quality. It is about included accessories. Polarity neutral. It could be convenience_value? No, accessory condition? Hmm.

Potential issue: Claim 1 title: "needs more items to assist in installation process" maybe primary usability_installation, secondary installation_accessories. Polarity negative. Good.

Potential issue: Claim 2 "My install was perfect for my phone." primary usability_installation, secondary ease_of_use? Could secondary installation_difficulty? Since positive, ease of use. The secondary list has ease_of_use. Good.

Potential issue: Claim 4 installation difficulty vs ease_of_use. Negative: installation_difficulty. Good.

Potential issue: Claim 5 general_performance positive. Could be reliability_durability/general_durability because "no issues so far" indicates durability. But "no issues whatsoever so far" ambiguous. Function_performance general_performance seems fine. If we choose reliability_durability/general_durability? "no issues whatsoever so far" often reliability. But taxonomy has function_performance general_performance. Hmm. "one on my phone seems to have no issues whatsoever so far" It's about performance/function. Could be general_performance. I'd keep.

Need maybe include claim "my install was perfect" and title "needs more items..." Both from same review. Fine.

Need ensure JSON valid no extra text. Use double quotes. No markdown. Final only.

But let's re-evaluate possibility of claim "both we attempted to install ... did not have same easy installation even though we followed exact same process and directions" Could also be product_quality/defective_on_arrival? The two protectors did not install easily, maybe defective. But taxonomy: installation_difficulty is direct. Good.

Could include "Seems like the quality on the other two screens wasn’t the same as mine" as product_quality/material_build_quality. yes.

Could include "Attempted to make contact for replacement..." as other_unknown/uncategorized negative? The instruction says if no supported product claim exists, empty list. Customer service issue not product. Omit. But "Attempted to make contact for replacement" implies they want replacement because product issue. But already captured quality/install. No need.

Need final JSON. Use exact source_text substrings. Note source text includes newline after title. Evidence for title no newline. Good.

Let's craft final.

Ensure "wasn’t" curly apostrophe. In JSON, Unicode allowed. Need not escape. "husband’s" curly. Good.

Order maybe as in source: title claim, install perfect, 3 included, both attempted, no issues, quality other two. That is fine.

Double-check schema: claims items require primary_topic, secondary_topic, polarity, evidence_span. AdditionalProperties false at object and claim. Polarity enum. Good.

Final.
